{
  "summary": "Adds Cap'n Proto schemas and C++ proxy serialization code for `interfaces::Chain` and `interfaces::Handler`, exposing `interfaces::Chain` via IPC on `bitcoin-node`. It also updates the `src/ipc/libmultiprocess` subtree and suppresses `-Wc++23-lambda-attributes` warnings when compiling interface wrappers.",
  "problem": "Currently, `interfaces::Chain` can only be invoked within the same process. Separate executables, such as an isolated `bitcoin-wallet` process, cannot access node chain state, submit transactions, or register chain notification handlers over IPC.",
  "evidence": [
    "PR description: 'This PR is a dependency of #10102 which allows the wallet code to run in a separate process and use the `Chain` interface.'",
    "PR description: 'The changes in this PR allow a `bitcoin-node` process to be controlled over a socket. The socket can either be an UNIX socket created by specifying the `-ipcbind` option, or it can be a socketpair created by a controlling process and passed to `bitcoin-node` via the `-ipcfd=<n>` with a file descriptor number.'"
  ],

      "#19460",
      "#19461"

  "card": "Adds Cap'n Proto definitions and proxy wrappers exposing the `interfaces::Chain` and `interfaces::Handler` interfaces over IPC on `bitcoin-node`. Currently, the chain interface is only callable within the same process, blocking multiprocess process separation. This PR is an explicit prerequisite for #10102 and #19460 to run the wallet in a separate process.",

result.summary: Adds Cap'n Proto schemas and C++ proxy serialization code for `interfaces::Chain` and `interfaces::Handler`, exposing `interfaces::Chain` via IPC on `bitcoin-node`. It also updates the `src/ipc/libmultiprocess` subtree and suppresses `-Wc++23-lambda-attributes` warnings when compiling interface wrappers.
result.problem: Currently, `interfaces::Chain` can only be invoked within the same process. Separate executables, such as an isolated `bitcoin-wallet` process, cannot access node chain state, submit transactions, or register chain notification handlers over IPC.
evidence: PR description: 'This PR is a dependency of #10102 which allows the wallet code to run in a separate process and use the `Chain` interface.'

PR description: 'The changes in this PR allow a `bitcoin-node` process to be controlled over a socket. The socket can either be an UNIX socket created by specifying the `-ipcbind` option, or it can be a socketpair created by a controlling process and passed to `bitcoin-node` via the `-ipcfd=<n>` with a file descriptor number.'
result.scope_notes: A significant portion of the diff is a subtree update to `src/ipc/libmultiprocess` along with its test harness and CI configuration.
result.changed_since_previous: Includes an updated `libmultiprocess` subtree sync and adds a commit suppressing `-Wc++23-lambda-attributes` warnings during interface compilation.
result.card: Adds Cap'n Proto definitions and proxy wrappers exposing the `interfaces::Chain` and `interfaces::Handler` interfaces over IPC on `bitcoin-node`. Currently, the chain interface is only callable within the same process, blocking multiprocess process separation. This PR is an explicit prerequisite for #10102 and #19460 to run the wallet in a separate process.

risk.why: Serialization bugs or memory leaks in IPC proxy code could cause node crashes or miscommunications when running multiprocess nodes.
